Supersymmetric solutions of \(N=2\), \(D=4\) minimal supergravity, both in the ungauged and gauged cases, can be systematically classified according to the fraction of supersymmetry they preserve. In this setting, one distinguishes solutions that preserve, for example, one quarter or one half of the available supersymmetry, since the amount of preserved supersymmetry strongly constrains the geometry and the accompanying bosonic fields.

The classification is carried out using techniques from spinorial geometry. This approach treats Killing spinors in a canonical way by using the action of the relevant gauge and Lorentz symmetry groups to simplify their form. Once representative spinors have been chosen, the Killing spinor equations can be translated into algebraic and differential conditions on the metric, gauge fields, and associated geometric structures. This makes it possible to organize the possible supersymmetric backgrounds in a systematic and efficient manner.

For minimal ungauged supergravity and for its gauged counterpart, the analysis separates the solutions into different classes, most notably time-like and null classes, depending on the causal nature of the vector bilinear constructed from the Killing spinors. In the gauged theory, particular attention is given to the \(1/2\)-supersymmetric time-like case. Under a reasonable simplifying assumption in this sector, the complete local form of all supersymmetric solutions can be derived. This provides an explicit description of the metric and gauge field configurations compatible with the required amount of supersymmetry.

The classification yields not only a unified understanding of previously known supersymmetric backgrounds, but also leads to new examples. In particular, both \(1/4\)-supersymmetric and \(1/2\)-supersymmetric solutions are found. These new backgrounds enlarge the known landscape of supersymmetric configurations in four-dimensional minimal supergravity and illustrate the usefulness of spinorial geometry as a constructive method.

Among the new solutions are gravitational waves propagating on bubbles of nothing in \(\mathrm{AdS}_4\). These geometries combine wave-like excitations with bubble-of-nothing structures in an anti-de Sitter spacetime, providing an interesting class of supersymmetric backgrounds in the gauged theory. Such examples demonstrate that the classification is not merely formal, but can reveal physically and geometrically novel solutions.

This work presents a systematic classification of supersymmetric solutions of four-dimensional \(N=2\) minimal supergravity, both in the ungauged theory and in the gauged theory with a negative cosmological constant. The analysis is organized according to the fraction of supersymmetry preserved by the bosonic background and is carried out using spinorial geometry techniques, which put the Killing spinor equations into canonical algebraic and differential forms. This approach makes it possible to reduce the problem of solving the supersymmetry conditions to the study of a small number of representative spinors and their associated geometric structures.

For the ungauged theory, the supersymmetric backgrounds are recovered in the standard time-like and null classes. The Killing spinor equations determine the metric and Maxwell field in terms of underlying geometric data, reproducing the known local forms of the supersymmetric solutions. The classification also identifies the enhancement conditions under which a solution preserves a larger fraction of supersymmetry, up to the maximally supersymmetric cases.

For the gauged theory, where the cosmological constant introduces new geometric possibilities, the classification is more intricate. The solutions are again separated according to the causal character of the Killing vector constructed from spinor bilinears and according to whether they preserve \(1/4\), \(1/2\), or all of the supersymmetry. The work derives the general local form of all supersymmetric configurations. In the time-like \(1/2\)-supersymmetric sector, the classification is completed under a mild technical assumption, allowing the full set of local solutions in this class to be written explicitly.

The resulting geometries include both previously known solutions and new families of supersymmetric backgrounds. Among the new configurations are \(1/4\)- and \(1/2\)-supersymmetric solutions describing gravitational waves propagating on bubbles of nothing in \(\mathrm{AdS}_4\). These examples illustrate the richness of the gauged theory: the interplay between the Maxwell field, the negative cosmological constant, and the spinorial constraints permits nontrivial space-times that have no direct analogue in the simplest ungauged setting.

Overall, the classification provides a complete local description of supersymmetric solutions of \(N=2\), \(D=4\) minimal ungauged and gauged supergravity, subject only to the stated mild assumption in the time-like half-supersymmetric gauged case. It clarifies the possible fractions of preserved supersymmetry, gives explicit geometric conditions for supersymmetry enhancement, and supplies new examples of supersymmetric \(\mathrm{AdS}_4\) backgrounds, thereby extending the known landscape of solutions in four-dimensional supergravity.

counterfactuals.output: We classify supersymmetric solutions of minimal \(N=2, D=4\) supergravity, both ungauged and gauged, using the spinorial geometry method. By representing Killing spinors as differential forms and exploiting local Lorentz and gauge transformations, we reduce the Killing spinor equations to canonical algebraic and differential systems. In the ungauged theory, the analysis reproduces the standard timelike and null classes, yielding the Israel–Wilson–Perjés-type geometries and pp-wave solutions. In the gauged theory, the cosmological constant and \(U(1)\) gauging modify the spinor orbits and impose additional geometric constraints, leading to the corresponding AdS generalizations, including timelike fibrations over three-dimensional base spaces and null wave-like configurations. counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main results of a study on supersymmetric solutions of four-dimensional N=2 minimal supergravity, including both ungauged and gauged cases.
counterfactuals.output:
The study gives a local classification of bosonic supersymmetric backgrounds of four-dimensional \(N=2\) minimal supergravity, treating both the ungauged theory and the theory with a gauging/Fayet–Iliopoulos term, i.e. with negative cosmological constant.

## General strategy

The analysis starts from the Killing spinor equation and constructs spinor bilinears: a scalar, a pseudoscalar, a vector, and two-forms. These bilinears obey differential and algebraic identities that strongly constrain the metric and Maxwell field. The solutions naturally split according to the causal character of the Killing vector built from the spinor:

1. **Timelike class**: the Killing vector is timelike on an open region.
2. **Null class**: the Killing vector is everywhere null.

The Killing spinor equations, together with the Bianchi identity and Maxwell equation, imply most or all of the bosonic equations of motion, so solving the reduced system yields supersymmetric solutions.

---

# Ungauged \(N=2\) minimal supergravity

The ungauged theory is ordinary Einstein–Maxwell theory with zero cosmological constant, restricted to configurations admitting a Killing spinor.

## Timelike class

All timelike supersymmetric solutions are of Israel–Wilson–Perjés type. Locally the metric can be written as

\[
ds^2 = |V|^2 (dt+\omega)^2 - |V|^{-2} d\vec{x}^{\,2},
\]

where \(V\) is a complex harmonic function on flat \(\mathbb{R}^3\),

\[
\nabla^2 V = 0,
\]

and the one-form \(\omega\) is determined by \(V\) through a first-order equation of the schematic form

\[
\nabla \times \omega
\sim i\left( V \nabla \bar V - \bar V \nabla V \right).
\]

The Maxwell field is also fixed by \(V\). This class includes the standard supersymmetric Reissner–Nordström black holes, multi-centre Majumdar–Papapetrou solutions, and more general stationary BPS Einstein–Maxwell geometries.

A key point is that the entire local solution is encoded in a harmonic function on \(\mathbb{R}^3\).

## Null class

The null supersymmetric solutions are gravitational/electromagnetic waves. The metric is of pp-wave type, with a covariantly constant or recurrent null Killing vector. The Maxwell field is null and aligned with the wave direction.

Thus, in the ungauged theory, supersymmetry allows essentially two types of local geometries:

- stationary BPS solutions governed by harmonic functions;
- null pp-wave-type solutions.

---

# Gauged \(N=2\) minimal supergravity

In the gauged case the theory contains a cosmological constant

\[
\Lambda = -3 g^2,
\]

so the maximally supersymmetric vacuum is \(AdS_4\). The gauging modifies the Killing spinor equation and substantially changes the local form of the solutions.

Again, the classification splits into timelike and null classes.

## Timelike class

For timelike supersymmetric solutions, the metric can be written as a fibration over a three-dimensional base space. A common canonical form is

\[
ds^2 =
-4 |b|^2 (dt+\sigma)^2
+ |b|^{-2}
\left[
dz^2 + e^{2\Phi} dw d\bar w
\right],
\]

where \(b\) is a complex function, \(\Phi\) is a real function, and \(\sigma\) is a one-form on the three-dimensional base. The Maxwell field is determined by the same data.

Unlike the ungauged case, the base is not generally flat, and the functions do not simply obey harmonic equations. Instead, supersymmetry reduces the problem to a coupled system of nonlinear differential equations for \(b\), \(\Phi\), and \(\sigma\). Solving these equations gives all local timelike supersymmetric solutions of minimal gauged supergravity.

This timelike class contains many important examples, including:

- \(AdS_4\);
- supersymmetric Reissner–Nordström–AdS-type solutions;
- rotating supersymmetric AdS black holes in special limits;
- magnetic and dyonic BPS configurations;
- geometries with nontrivial fibration structure over curved three-dimensional bases.

A major result is that the gauged classification generalizes the harmonic-function structure of the ungauged theory to a more intricate curved-base system controlled by the gauge coupling \(g\).

## Null class

The null supersymmetric solutions of the gauged theory are AdS generalizations of pp-waves. They are often described as Siklos or Kundt-type waves propagating on an \(AdS_4\) background. A typical form is conformal to a pp-wave metric,

\[
ds^2 =
\frac{1}{g^2 x^2}
\left[
-2\,du\,dv + dx^2 + dz^2 + H(u,x,z)\,du^2
\right],
\]

with possible accompanying null Maxwell fields. The profile functions are constrained by reduced linear or partially linear field equations.

These solutions represent gravitational and electromagnetic waves in anti-de Sitter space preserving some supersymmetry.

---

# Main conclusions

The study establishes a complete local classification of supersymmetric bosonic solutions of four-dimensional \(N=2\) minimal supergravity.

The key results are:

1. **Supersymmetric solutions split into timelike and null classes**, according to the causal nature of the Killing vector constructed from the Killing spinor.

2. **In the ungauged theory**, the timelike class is completely described by complex harmonic functions on flat \(\mathbb{R}^3\), giving the Israel–Wilson–Perjés family. The null class consists of pp-wave-type solutions.

3. **In the gauged theory**, the timelike class is described by a fibration over a three-dimensional base, governed by a coupled system of differential equations for a complex scalar, a conformal factor, and a one-form. This class includes \(AdS_4\) and many BPS AdS black-hole-like and solitonic geometries.

4. **The null gauged solutions** are AdS wave geometries, generalizing pp-waves to the presence of a negative cosmological constant.

5. The classification shows how the introduction of gauging deforms the simple harmonic-function structure of ungauged BPS solutions into a richer nonlinear geometric system.

counterfactuals.prompt: What are the key findings of a classification of 1/4- and 1/2-BPS solutions in N=2 four-dimensional minimal gauged supergravity using spinorial geometry?
counterfactuals.output:
Key findings of the spinorial-geometry classification of \(1/4\)- and \(1/2\)-BPS solutions in \(N=2,\,D=4\) minimal gauged supergravity include:

- **Systematic use of spinorial geometry:**  
  The Killing spinor equations are simplified by using local Lorentz/gauge transformations to put Killing spinors into canonical forms. This turns the supersymmetry conditions into tractable algebraic and differential constraints on the metric and Maxwell field.

- **Complete local classification of \(1/4\)-BPS backgrounds:**  
  Solutions preserving one real quarter of the supersymmetry are organized into canonical classes, typically distinguished by the causal nature of the Killing vector constructed from the Killing spinor — timelike or null. The resulting geometries are described by a reduced set of functions satisfying differential equations.

- **Recovery and extension of known supersymmetric solutions:**  
  The classification includes known supersymmetric configurations of minimal gauged supergravity, such as AdS-related geometries, supersymmetric black-hole-type solutions, magnetic/electric configurations, and wave-like solutions in AdS.

- **Classification of \(1/2\)-BPS solutions:**  
  Imposing a second independent Killing spinor strongly restricts the geometry and gauge field. The allowed half-supersymmetric backgrounds fall into a small number of local classes, including:
  - locally maximally supersymmetric \(\mathrm{AdS}_4\),
  - product-type geometries such as \(\mathrm{AdS}_2 \times H^2\) in appropriate flux backgrounds,
  - AdS wave/Siklos-type solutions,
  - other special limits of the quarter-BPS families.

- **No genuinely \(3/4\)-BPS solutions:**  
  A key result is that any solution preserving more than half of the supersymmetry is forced to be maximally supersymmetric. Thus there are no backgrounds preserving exactly \(3/4\) of the supersymmetry.

- **Maximally supersymmetric solution:**  
  The unique maximally supersymmetric solution of minimal gauged \(N=2\), \(D=4\) supergravity is locally \(\mathrm{AdS}_4\) with vanishing Maxwell field.

Overall, the classification shows that spinorial geometry gives an efficient and complete local description of supersymmetric bosonic backgrounds in minimal gauged four-dimensional supergravity, with \(1/2\)-BPS solutions being highly constrained and any enhancement beyond half supersymmetry leading directly to \(\mathrm{AdS}_4\).

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a paper abstract about classifying supersymmetric solutions by preserved supersymmetry fraction in minimal ungauged and gauged D=4 supergravity.
counterfactuals.output: We review and systematize the classification of supersymmetric bosonic solutions in minimal \(D=4\) supergravity, both ungauged and gauged, according to the fraction of supersymmetry preserved. The analysis is based on the Killing spinor equations and their associated bilinear structures, which distinguish timelike and null supersymmetric geometries and strongly constrain the metric and gauge-field configurations. In the ungauged theory, solutions preserving one quarter of the supersymmetry fall into the standard timelike Israel–Wilson–Perjés class or null pp-wave–type geometries, while enhancement to one half or full supersymmetry imposes additional integrability conditions leading to special subclasses, including Minkowski space, Bertotti–Robinson-type backgrounds, and maximally supersymmetric plane waves. In the gauged theory, the negative cosmological constant and graviphoton gauging modify the Killing spinor equation and lead to supersymmetric AdS geometries, including timelike fibrations over three-dimensional base spaces and null wave solutions. Supersymmetry enhancement again yields strong restrictions, with maximally supersymmetric configurations including \(AdS_4\) and other homogeneous limits where allowed. By organizing known local solution families by their preserved supersymmetry fraction, the paper clarifies the relation between spinorial isotropy groups, geometric structure, and field equations, and provides a unified framework for identifying BPS backgrounds in minimal four-dimensional supergravity. This classification is relevant for the study of supersymmetric black holes, gravitational instantons, AdS/CFT backgrounds, and the broader structure of supersymmetric solution spaces.
